end.summary:
Pari practised naming common non-metals and identifying their states.
They explained uses of oxygen, helium, graphite, nitrogen, chlorine and iodine.
They connected oxygen with breathing and medical oxygen, and nitrogen with food packaging.
They identified iodine crystals and graphite as solids; teach-back was not completed.
end.parentNote: Pari practised the uses and states of common non-metals by connecting each one to everyday examples, such as oxygen for breathing, helium in balloons, graphite in pencils, nitrogen in chip packets and chlorine in water treatment. Their explanations used relevant examples and observations. The teach-back was not completed because the lesson ended; no recorded mix-up remained uncorrected. At home, ask them to sort the listed non-metals into solid, liquid and gas, then state one use for each.
